fine_trace.code: unsigned char s[1024]; ssize_t len = hpeek(hfile, s, 18);
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are read into the stack buffer s via hpeek, with len set to the number of bytes actually available.
The input is passed to parse_tabbed_text which classifies each tab-separated column and fills the local columns array with type characters.
Each column type is written into the 24-byte columns buffer; ncolumns is incremented after each write.
The loop breaks when ncolumns reaches column_len-1 (23), so columns[23]='\0' is the last write and stays in bounds.

fine_trace.code: for (i = 0; columns[i] != '\0'; i++) { if (pattern[i] == '+') return i; if (! (columns[i] == pattern[i] || pattern[i] == 'Z')) return 0; }
fine_trace.note: colmatch reads pattern[i] for i up to strlen(columns). For the short patterns like "iiiiii", "Ziiiii", "Ziiii", and "Zii+", if columns has more characters than the pattern, pattern[i] reads past the end of the string literal, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.

The SAM pattern is long enough, but the subsequent shorter patterns ("iiiiii", "Ziiiii", "Ziiii", "Zii+") are tried when the SAM match fails, and these can over-read the pattern string when columns is longer than the pattern.

If columns has 7 or more characters, colmatch reads pattern[6] which is the NUL terminator of the 6-character pattern, and then continues reading pattern[7] and beyond if columns has more characters, causing an out-of-bounds read.
Similarly, if columns has 7 or more characters, colmatch reads past the end of the 6-character pattern "Ziiiii".
If columns has 6 or more characters, colmatch reads past the end of the 5-character pattern "Ziiii".
If columns has 5 or more characters, colmatch reads past the end of the 4-character pattern "Zii+", causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
